package.name: statgrab
package.summary: PHP bindings for libstatgrab: CPU, memory, disk, network, and process metrics.
package.description:
PHP bindings for libstatgrab (https://libstatgrab.org), the cross-platform system-statistics library. Reads CPU usage, memory and swap, disk I/O, filesystem space and inode counts, network interface counters, page-in/out, process tables, logged-in users, and host metadata. Works on glibc Linux, musl, macOS, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, and Solaris.
Two API surfaces ship in parallel: a procedural one matching the original 2006 PECL release (sg_cpu_percent_usage, sg_memory_stats, sg_process_stats, ...) and a Statgrab class with method-based access and class constants for sort orders, process states, and duplex modes. Both surfaces emit E_WARNING and return false on libstatgrab errors; the OO surface throws on argument-count violations. sg_error_details() returns array{code,errno,message,arg} from libstatgrab (or false when no error is pending); the OO surface exposes the same shape via Statgrab::errorDetails().
The repo also ships a vendored libstatgrab 0.92.1 with one local patch fixing an sg_destroy_globals off-by-one that leaks the user-stats vector at process exit (submitted upstream, not yet released). Configure with --with-statgrab=bundled to statically link the patched copy and ship the leak fix without waiting on system packages.
Requires libstatgrab >= 0.92 and PHP >= 8.0 (NTS).
package.notes:
Correctness fixes for error constants, result keys, and process stats.
- Statgrab::ERROR_UNSUPPORTED is 44, matching libstatgrab's sg_error enum (was 41, SG_ERROR_MACHCALL). - Duplicate device or interface names in diskio, network, and iface results no longer overwrite earlier rows; collisions use numeric keys. - sg_error_details() returns the code/errno/message/arg array when a libstatgrab error is pending (it always returned false). - sg_process_stats() sorts a caller-owned copy instead of libstatgrab's shared vector, and a negative limit throws ValueError (0 means all). - Cold sg_cpu_percent_usage() diff-source calls return the first sample row instead of false with a misleading warning. - Statgrab::cpu() reflection shows Statgrab::CPU_PERCENT_ENTIRE as the default. - A failed initial sg_snapshot() at startup emits a notice naming the libstatgrab error.
See CHANGELOG.md for the full list.
